items.title: Streamer Loses 11 Hours of GTA 6 Progress After Accidentally Turning Off Their PS5, Gets Swatted Immediately Afterwards

JasonTheWeen, a steamer with 1.3 million followers on YouTube, lost 11 hours and a whole chapter of progress in GTA 6 after accidentally turning their PS5 off.

After realizing what had happened, the clearly emotional JasonTheWeen broke down in tears. "I'm not doing this s**t," he says, sobbing. "Oh my god. Oh my f***ing god. F***ing 11 hours!"

Then, calling who we assume is his channel editor or manager, JasonTheWeen pleaded for help. “I'm streaming right now, I'm doing my GTA marathon, and I was 11 hours in and I accidentally turned off my PS5 and lost all my progress,” he said in a clip posted to social media. “Is there any way you could contact Rockstar? Maybe they can get me back to Chapter 2? I don’t know what you can do. I don't know what to do.”

JasonTheWeen is then told to send over all the info he has so he can reach out to Rockstar and “see what happens.”

At this point, the cuffs were slapped onto Lucia’s wrists and the game flash-forwarded back to the present day where GTA 6’s co-protagonist continued her consultation with her correctional counselor in Leonida Penitentiary, and the story launched gloriously into the game’s first chapter.

items.title: Looking for free guns and body armor in GTA 6? Try the trunks of cop cars
items.summary:
Remember how stealing a cop car in the older GTA games used to get you a free shotgun? Well, turns out Vice City's police force is even better armed. If you need some extra guns quickly, particularly shotguns and assault rifles, filching them from the trunk of a police car is a great method, though obviously it comes with certain risks.

You might have realised, but stealing cars in GTA 6 is significantly more complicated than previous games, especially if they're alarmed. Thankfully, this doesn't apply to any police pickup trucks like the Bravado Bison the cops sometimes use, which you'll spot occasionally both in rural areas and in the city 

With the police pickups, you can simply climb onto the bed at the back and open the storage crate, grabbing any weapons and ammo inside, including other potential items like Stun Guns, without setting off any alarms.

For proper police cruisers, though, their trunks are alarmed along with the doors, meaning you'll need a tool to deal with them, the slim jim , which you get during the "Moses" mission in Chapter 2. If you slim jim the door of the cop car and get inside, the trunk will unlock, so you can head around the back, interact to open it, and steal whatever's in the boot without tackling the alarm, whether it be an assault rifle, shotgun, or even body armor.

items.title: Refueling cars in GTA 6 is barely necessary, but there's much better reason to visit garages
items.summary:
Having to refuel cars in GTA 6 was weirdly one of the most talked about features before launch—I guess people didn't like the idea of having to pull over for gas while being chased by half the Vice City's police department. But the reality is that refuelling cars is something you'll barely find yourself doing.

When your ride does run low on fuel, you can find a gas station on the map via the gas pump symbols:

Pull up to a pump close enough to see the prompt for "Services" Select "Refuel" (It will also display the $ cost) Press the interact button You'll see Jason or Lucia picking up the pump handle Hold down the button shown in the lower right corner to refuel When you're done, you'll see Jason or Lucia replace the pump handle You'll be back in your car Easy, right? And you'll barely have to do it since, just like real life, cars can go quite a long time without refuelling if they have a full tank, even if you're going over 60mph, which I assume you are. Note that if you steal a stranger's car, their tank may nearly be empty already.

If you're driving an electric car, check the map for recharging stations. Pull up close to one, select "Charge Vehicle," and it'll display the cost. You'll see a quick scene of the readout on the charging station filling the battery to 100%, and when it's done, you can drive away.

items.title: Bank your cash in GTA 6, but always keep a few hundred on you—you never know when you'll need it
items.summary:
Cash is king in GTA 6 , and Rockstar has come up with some new systems to manage your finances, from a secret stash under the floorboards to an honest-to-goodness interest-bearing savings account.

But you need to be careful with your money, especially at the start of the game when even a few hundred bucks can make or break you. While wandering around Leonida, strangers might try to rob you (big mistake), but more importantly, if you die or get arrested, you'll be penalized a few hundred dollars. There's also a $20k limit to how much you can keep on your person as you gradually accumulate more and more through play.

The solution? Stash your cash frequently. During the initial chapters of the game, you won't have a bank account, but you can store your money in your house in Key Lento by simply stashing it under the floorboards in the bedroom. This will mean you have a little money tucked away, and won't lose it when you die or get busted by the cops. . 

Remember, you can also stash stolen goods like jewelry, drugs, and marked bills from robberies in the trunk of your car. Even if your car gets impounded by the fuzz, you'll be able to recover that contraband from your trunk later on and sell it. Don't stash goods in a car you don't own, though: you might lose it if you lose that car.

items.summary:
GTA 6 has officially launched in all time zones, and while Rockstar has been marketing its heart out for what feels like a lifetime, one fast-food chain waited until launch to join in on the fun.

Burger Shot, a parody of Burger King, has been a staple of the Grand Theft Auto series since the original Vice City game. Now, Burger King in Belgium is "taking back what they’re owed" by turning an iconic Burger Shot offering into a real-life product: the HeartWhopper.

The 'heart' of it all isn’t about how much Burger King loves GTA — it refers to how likely this thing is to give you a heart attack.

While Burger Shot first appeared in Vice City, the 'Heart Stopper' burger was a big part of the background world in GTA 4. In-game, you hear commercials for the burger with customers dialing 9-1-1 as they eat. The burger’s slogan? “Oh, I think my heart just stopped!”

Just like the super-sized in-game product, Burger King’s HeartWhopper features a whopping seven beef patties in addition to the usual lettuce, tomato, and onion slices.

It's worth noting you can't simply walk into a Burger King in Belgium and buy a HeartWhopper from the menu. Rather, you can win one through a two-week social media competition where you share a video clip of yourself eating a burger from the in-game restaurant and Burger King Belgium picks its favorite each day.

Characters aren't individual players. You can create dozens of characters on your account if you want to, but I'd guess most people didn't do that. Breaking into cars

If it's a keyless car, you won't be able to hotwire it or drive it away—again, more on that below. If you smash a window on an alarmed car, the alarm will sound, which can attract attention.

items.title: How to get safe codes in GTA 6

GTA 6 safe codes will let you unlock sealed loot containers in the main story, but also during the lucrative robbery activity, which sees you knock over gang hideouts, banks, and other cash and contraband rich institutions.

The safe codes you need in the main story or specific missions are given to you, but in order to get a safe code during a robbery (and you'll need to because they're randomised), you have two main options:

Find the code written down on the premises Interrogate an employee to get it First off, you can sometimes find the code written on something inside the store or bank, like a note on a board in the back office perhaps, or maybe a guard you've incapacitated is carrying it—press L3 and R3 to activate Focus Mode and help you find it.

You can also get the code by interrogating employees. Aim your weapon at them and use the "Threaten" or "Safe Code?" prompt shown on the screen to force them to give you the information. In certain robberies, this will also force cashiers to empty the register, as in previous GTA games.

items.title: How to reach 6 stars in GTA 6

As with the previous games, the highest star levels are reserved for trespassing in an airport and stealing a passenger jet, or heading to a military base and hijacking an APC. And, as always, five stars will see a tank dispatched.

But you can only get to six stars if you cause mass destruction and loss of life. The only way we were able to get a six star wanted level in GTA 6 was by stealing a tank from a military base and blowing up other tanks and vehicles. 

Just keep this in mind:

At six stars, you'll no longer be able to lose heat or wanted level. You can run but you can't hide because once you're at six stars, the law will never stop hunting you. This means your only way out is to die, essentially. It's also worth considering that killing all of those cops could impact your criminal profile quite severely.

items.title: World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling

I don't play video games regularly anymore. Not because I've lost interest in them, but because I no longer make the time, the premium on which has seemed to exponentiate with age. I realised, however, in 2019 that I was a kind of sleeper agent: whenever I heard the opening notes of Legends of Azeroth , the original World of Warcraft login screen music, I would feel the reactivation of a latent part of my mind laid down when I was 10 years old. And so, like a form of possession, whenever Blizzard announces a new legacy iteration of the original WoW, no downpayment in time nor money is too great to prevent me from returning.

Here I am, then, at the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever, seven years after Blizzard first revived the original 2004 game with World of Warcraft Classic in 2019. Once more I set foot on Durotar, to spend as much time as I can levelling up a new Orc Warrior before I am forcibly unplugged by either my boss or, more likely, my wife, and so far it's been a welcome return to some of the frictional - but more involving and consequential - socialising that WoW's decades of updates had previously sanded down.

The player in the advert always does pretty well for 20 seconds, but ahhhh, then they get just a tiny bit overconfident, mistime how long it'll take them to erode the health of an ogre midboss, and: bam!

Show me one of those ads, and I'll always watch to the end in the hope that this time, the protagonist will Study The Blade, conquer their harmatia, and slay the damn ogre. I've never actually played any of the mobile shooters in question, mind you. I'm far too cultured for that, you dope! Except that I've just been playing the demo for Korridor, which is supposedly "based off" of the ads, but might as well be one of the games they're promoting, for all I know.
items.t: Korridor turns those Youtube ads for vertical mobile shooters into a new, "deeply strategic" genre, and I can't decide if it's lying

items.title: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish
items.summary:
At this point the tragedy of Driv3r , or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized tupperware container.

A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and even 22 years before GTA 6 's idolising reviews , that was no small promise; Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world, either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were about to wheel into the showroom.

You likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. Six hours later, I am here to tell you: it was.

It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto . Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6 , which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes , that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

It wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption . Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5 .

items.title: Break up and re-commodify a fallen Earth in Steel Gullet, a satisfyingly funereal factory puzzler that really loves thermodynamics
items.summary:
It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game. Out now on PC, Steel Gullet is a factory engineering puzzler that, while notable for its meticulous interest in thermodynamics, broadly compares to the foundational work of Zachtronics , together with more recent and focussed conveyor belt wranglers such as Modulus . Resources come in, and you arrange machines on a grid to transform them into something else, before sliding them into an output hopper.

The difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth. Your resources are the refuse of a bygone human civilisation: knots of concrete and rebar, flaccid rubber hose and splintered plank, that must be separated out before you can manufacture anything.
